Analysis:
Average Overtime per capita is generally less than the state.  There will be peaks that do not match the state based on being a production facility.  The majority of overtime is earned by our production employees.  Our production employees represent over 50% of our staff.  This also accounts for the % of employees receiving overtime.
The Overtime Cost for the agency will fluctuate based on business needs.  One such pattern of high overtime is during the end of the fiscal year as a high volume of jobs are ordered by our customers. 
Action Steps:
We regularly monitor overtime and the ability to meet the needs of our customers.

Employee Survey “Employee Commitment” Ratings
Analysis:
Agency averages for questions 9 and 12 are slightly below the state averages.  Agency average for question 3 is equal to the state average.
Agency average for question 9 is slightly below the state average of 3.4. More than a quarter of our employees feel that they seldom or never receive recognition for a job well done.

Action Steps:
The agency has focused on open communication of its goals, its successes, areas needing improvement, and the direction the agency is going.  This information is shared to all employees via all staff meetings and department meetings.
Our agency is developing a recognition program that will incorporate individual thanks as well as traditional forms of recognition.  The program is to be in place by the end of November.

Department of Printing

Analysis:
There was a slight decrease in turnover during the second half or the fiscal year.
The majority of our resignations come from our entry level production employees.
Action Steps:
The agency has addressed one cause of the entry level production resignations by reviewing and changing the wage structure for those positions.  The positions are physically demanding so some turnover is to be expected. 
In addition, the agency is developing a recognition program that will incorporate individual thanks as well as traditional forms of recognition.
